text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Thursday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Co-chairman of the Council of Ministers, Haris Silajdzic, said at donors' conference in Brussels that peace in Bosnia was never as dependent on economic development as it is now.
- Moslem-Croat federation premier Edhem Bicakcic said industrial production in Bosnia is at 25 percent of its pre-war level.

- U.S. special envoy Robert Gelbard suggested in Brussels that donors set aside special funds for the Bosnian Serb entity, which would be delivered only after the Serbs comply with the Dayton peace agreement.
- The chairman of the Bosnian presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, met Spanish Defence Minister Eduard Serr and praised the contribution of Spanish soldiers to the NATO-led Stabilisation Force.
- Association of war invalids, in an open letter sent to the country's leadership, requested that soldiers' bank books in the Moslem-Croat federation be revised.

- Federal interior ministry representatives failed to sign an agreement on formation of a joint Moslem-Croat police force in the town of Travnik, due to disagreement over the name of the police district.
- Mirza Hajric, aide to presidency chairman, says a meeting between Izetbegovic and the Croatian President Franjo Tudjman is expected in two weeks.

- Leaders of the ruling Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) and Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) in central town of Zepce signed an agreement on the peaceful return of Moslems and Croats to the area.
- Government statistics show 84 percent of small and 29 percent of middle-sized companies in the Moslem-Croat federation are privately owned.

- Deputy to the High Representative, Gerd Wagner, discussed the structure of local government with representatives of Moslem and Croat ruling parties in the Mostar region. Wagner said joint municipalities can only supervise municipal services and cannot replace city or cantonal authorities.

- Robert Frowick, head of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) mission in Bosnia, said the final list of voters who registered for local elections will be published on August 18. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
